sample_unit: patients (consecutive ID consultations for first positive blood culture)

links.outcome: Adequacy of ChatGPT-4 diagnosis, workup, and antibiotic plans versus ID consultants
links.effect: Diagnoses identical in 26 (59%); empirical therapy adequate in 28 (64%), harmful in 1 (2%); definitive therapy optimal in 16 (36%), harmful in 2 (5%); overall plans harmful in 7 (16%).
links.quote: Overall, management plans were considered optimal in only 1 patient, as satisfactory in 17 (39%), and as harmful in 7 (16%).

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety of ChatGPT-4 management plans against expert reference
links.effect: Only 1 plan optimal, 17 (39%) satisfactory, 7 (16%) harmful; diagnoses matched consultant in 59%.
links.quote: Overall, management plans were considered optimal in only 1 patient, as satisfactory in 17 (39%), and as harmful in 7 (16%).

links.outcome: Clinical harm potential of unverified chatbot recommendations
links.effect: Harmful management plans in 7 (16%) cases; authors conclude use without consultant input is hazardous.
links.quote: The use of ChatGPT-4 without consultant input remains hazardous when seeking expert medical advice in 2023, especially for severe IDs.

screen.reason: Prospective cohort evaluation of ChatGPT-4 performance on real-world infectious disease consultations for positive blood cultures, evaluated offline/simulated against human ID consultant plans without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
